page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core, yielding 32 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 124 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the c4d-standard-32 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier rankings. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by its Geekbench multi-core score and Passmark CPU score, which rank in the top 10% and top 25% respectively. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks fall into the average tier. The instance also shows average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and software compilation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-standard-32 offers high compute density per resource unit, making it highly effective for CPU-bound tasks that benefit from strong single-threaded execution and advanced vector instructions like AVX-512. The primary tradeoff is the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for large-scale local database hosting or heavy deep learning training. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, image and text processing, single-threaded data decompression, and light LLM inference using small models.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor configured with 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 124 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, as demonstrated by its high Geekbench and Passmark scores. While memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier, its excellent single-threaded decompression and image processing speeds make it highly efficient for compute-intensive workloads. The CPU architecture supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512, and features 32 MB of L3 cache, enhancing its capability for mathematical and cryptographic operations. It is well-suited for static web serving, text processing, and small-model LLM inference.
